notes.title: Dev Diary
notes.content:
Dev Diary: The Evolution of Cart Capers
A Wild Ride from Story to Competition
Hey everyone! We’re super excited to share the story behind the development of Cart Capers and how it transformed from a charming little neighborhood adventure into a full-blown, chaotic, multiplayer obstacle-racing game.

The Early Days: A Kid, a Cart, and a Dream
Originally, Cartness, as it was called back then, was a story-driven single-player game. You played as John, a determined ten-year-old trying to earn enough money to buy a bike. Players would help quirky neighbors with shopping errands, pushing a shopping cart through obstacle-filled streets. Each mission was designed to teach new mechanics like pushing, steering, doing wheelies, and jumping.
It was a colorful, heartwarming setup with lots of character interactions. We even had a rival character, Max, to spice things up.

Big Dreams: Adding Multiplayer and Open World
As the game evolved, we realized the core gameplay—riding a shopping cart through crazy obstacles—was just too much fun not to share with friends. So we expanded into multiplayer.
At one point, we dreamed big: a free-roam multiplayer city called Cart Capers City, where players could hang out, invite friends, practice tricks, and jump into matches together. The main menu was designed to look like a fridge full of post-it notes, and your "Core Controls" tutorial would be pinned right there on a sticky note.
We brainstormed modes like:
Capture the Flag (bumping into others to steal an item)
Trash Rush (collect and deposit trash items around the map)
Trials (brutal deathrun obstacle courses)
We also added environmental features like chasebreakers (shortcuts that collapse or close behind you) and chasers (dogs or security guards pursuing you).
While the idea was, and still is, interesting it was a tremendous level-design task that could have us bogged down for months. We had to take smaller steps first.

Reality Check: Refocusing on the Fun
As much as we loved the open-world idea, it didn’t fit the heart of the game. We wanted tight, exciting matches, not endless wandering.
So, we scrapped free-roam and story content entirely.
Now, Cart Capers is purely about racing, jumping, sabotaging, and surviving obstacle courses with friends. Quick matches, fast action, pure chaos.
Players jump straight into levels and race to the finish.
Two paths emerged:
Race Tracks: Pure speed, drift mastery, and tight steering.
Deathrun Courses: Trap-dodging obstacle gauntlets that test timing and guts.
Wheelie and jump mechanics became the heart of movement—simple to learn but endlessly tricky to master.
Sabotage or teamwork: Push rivals into traps or cooperate to survive the deadliest courses.
The streamlined focus makes every match thrilling, competitive, and hilarious.

Where We Are Now
Today, Cart Capers is a fast, fun, and skill-based multiplayer racer that’s easy to pick up but tough to master. We’re laser-focused on delivering that adrenaline rush of narrowly landing a jump, perfectly drifting a corner, or pushing your best friend straight into a pit trap.
Thanks for following along with our development journey. The path wasn’t always smooth, but just like in Cart Capers, a few bumps only made the ride more exciting. We can’t wait for you to jump in and race with us!
Stay tuned for more updates—and remember, keep those wheelies sharp!
Wishlist Cart Capers today and be ready for launch!
